record.paper_title: Finite translation generalized quadrangles: old results, new results, open problems
record.context_brief: Goodness of an egg or its dual
record.original_question: Given an egg O(n, 2n, q) and its translation dual O∗(n, 2n, q), is it always true that at least one of O or O∗ is good in the sense defined in the paper?

evidence.quote: 5. Is one of O(n, 2n, q) and O∗(n, 2n, q) always good?

The tangent spaces of an egg O(n, m, q), n = m, form an egg O∗(n, m, q) in the dual space of PG(2n+m−1, q). So in addition to T(n, m, q) there arises a TGQ T ∗(n, m, q). The egg O∗(n, m, q) = O∗ will be called the translation dual of O(n, m, q) = O.

An egg O = O(n, 2n, q), respectively a TGQ T(O), is called good at an element π ∈ O if for every two distinct elements π and π′ of O − {π} the (3n − 1)-dimensional space < π, π′, π > contains exactly qn + 1 elements of O; in such a case π is called a good element of O.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let q be a prime power and n a positive integer. Work inside the projective space PG(4n−1, q). An egg O = O(n, 2n, q) is a family of q^{2n} + 1 mutually disjoint (n−1)-dimensional subspaces of PG(4n−1, q) such that:
(E1) any three distinct elements of O span a (3n−1)-dimensional subspace; and
(E2) at every element π ∈ O there is a unique (3n−1)-dimensional subspace T_π, called the tangent space at π, that contains π and is disjoint from every other element of O.

The set of tangent spaces {T_π : π ∈ O}, viewed in the dual space PG(4n−1, q)*, again forms an egg, denoted O*(n, 2n, q) and called the translation dual of O.

An element π ∈ O is called good if, for every two distinct elements π′, π″ of O ∖ {π}, the (3n−1)-dimensional subspace ⟨π, π′, π″⟩ spanned by π, π′, π″ contains exactly q^n + 1 elements of O. The egg O is called good (at π) if some such element π exists; the same definition applies to O*.

Question: Is it true that for every egg O = O(n, 2n, q), at least one of O and its translation dual O* is good?
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this specific question was found. It is posed as an open problem in surveys on translation generalized quadrangles, and subsequent work (e.g., characterizations of good eggs and of elementary pseudo-caps, and the classification of eggs in PG(7,2)) addresses related questions but does not appear to settle whether at least one of an egg and its translation dual must always be good. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Characterisations of elementary pseudo-caps and good eggs
status_evidence.snippet: Thas showed that an egg in PG(4n-1, q), q odd, with two good elements is elementary; analogous results in even characteristic.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work characterizes good eggs but does not resolve whether one of O, O* must be good.

status_evidence.title: Generalised quadrangles VI: translation generalised quadrangles
status_evidence.snippet: Given an egg with associated TGQ, there is also a dual egg and so another TGQ, referred to as the translation dual.
status_evidence.claim: The translation dual construction is standard; the goodness comparison question is discussed as open.
